For people wondering why he used a fax machine, faxed communication have special 'value' under Australian law. (and in many other countries).

Back in the 70's and early 80's, back before everyone had home computers and photoshop and emails, faxes were the fastest way to send documents from one location to another.

At the time there were numerous court cases around the world, supported with evidence from major fax manufactures, that established in court that the document you send via fax is effectively identical to the document you receive. It was also established that faxes were very difficult, almost impossible, to tamper with or forge, or intercept, at least for 99.9% of the population.. (remember no photoshop)

These cases set a legal precedent. Faxed documents are considered almost as good as an original copy for legal purposes.

If you fax someone a contract, they sign it and fax it back to you, it's legally binding.

No such legal precedent has ever been set for email.

That's why lawyers and real estate agents still uses faxes to send each other documents. That's why doctors still fax prescriptions to pharmacies.

i.e. Sending it by fax makes it a legally binding document under Australian law, an email would be in a legal grey area.

TL/DR: He didn't use a fax because he technologically backwards. He did it because sending a resignation by email has no legal weight.
